answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by allocating work through a quadratic task auction. Each identity submits bids for jobs, but its effective capacity scales as the square root of total stake, so splitting one agent's capital across ten clones yields barely a third of the original throughput. At the epoch zenith, the protocol assembles an atlas of bids and routes each job along a trellis of verified channels, charging a routing fee per hop. A sybil pays duplicate stakes and fees for reduced capacity, making mass identity creation self-defeating.
